title: An outbreak of hypervitaminosis D associated with the overfortification of milk from a home-delivery dairy
authors: Blank S, Scanlon KS, Sinks TH, Lett S, Falk H
population: Cases of hypervitaminosis D diagnosed 1 January 1985 to 30 June 1991, identified from hospital discharge, laboratory and state health department data; case-control study of 33 cases and 93 controls
funder: not stated in the readable text; the article body is available only as page images, so the funding statement was not read. Authors are affiliated with the Epidemic Intelligence Service, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
result: Of 56 case patients identified, at least 41 were hospitalised and 2 died. Nineteen of 33 case patients had been customers of the implicated dairy; risk rose with consumption of its milk and was also associated with vitamin D supplement use. The authors conclude that overfortification of milk with vitamin D can lead to hypervitaminosis D with severe illness and death.
